question: Can the model forecast a river it has never seen?

settings.warning_rule: forecast > 95th percentile of the model's own forecasts for that basin and lead in the training years

lobo_w_nostatic.label: held out, weather only (no basin properties)

lobo_rf_w.label: held out, random forest (weather features + basin properties)

lstm_w_s0.label: in training: one LSTM for all 12 basins, past weather + basin properties (04_lstm_all.py, seed 0)

lobo_ref_w_nostatic.label: in training: one LSTM for all 12 basins, past weather only (this script, seed 0)

base_rf_w.label: in training: one random forest per basin, past weather (02_baselines.py)

flow_per_rain.what: share of the rain that reached the river (total flow / total rain) in the training, validation and test years; from the gauge, used only to describe a basin

what_goes_with_the_loss.what: Spearman rank correlation over the 12 basins between the NSE loss 1 day ahead (with basin properties) and a basin feature; 12 points only

findings: 1 day ahead, never-seen basin: median test NSE 0.216 with basin properties and 0.313 with weather only, against 0.434 when the basin was in training; 11 of 12 basins keep a positive NSE with properties, 11 of 12 with weather only, 11 of 12 for the random forest (median 0.329).

1 day ahead, loss from not having seen the basin (median over basins): +0.126 NSE with basin properties (11 of 12 basins lower, 9 by more than the typical seed range of 0.064, 11 below every single in-training seed); +0.043 with weather only (11 lower, 4 beyond the seed range); +0.040 for the random forest; largest loss 2.51 / 0.88 / 1.19.

1 day ahead, basin properties for a never-seen basin: no clear difference by the median rule - higher with properties in 4 of 12 basins, lower in 8; median difference -0.026 NSE, mean -0.129, difference of the medians -0.097 (typical seed range 0.064, Wilcoxon p = 0.266); for basins in training: no clear difference, higher with properties in 8 of 12, median difference +0.022.

1 day ahead, LSTM against the random forest, both never having seen the basin: the LSTM is higher in 2 of 12 basins with basin properties (median difference -0.043) and in 5 of 12 with weather only (-0.017).

2 days ahead, never-seen basin: median test NSE 0.114 with basin properties and 0.156 with weather only, against 0.284 when the basin was in training; 10 of 12 basins keep a positive NSE with properties, 11 of 12 with weather only, 11 of 12 for the random forest (median 0.177).

2 days ahead, loss from not having seen the basin (median over basins): +0.086 NSE with basin properties (11 of 12 basins lower, 7 by more than the typical seed range of 0.067, 9 below every single in-training seed); +0.034 with weather only (11 lower, 5 beyond the seed range); +0.006 for the random forest; largest loss 2.30 / 0.70 / 0.91.

2 days ahead, basin properties for a never-seen basin: no clear difference by the median rule - higher with properties in 4 of 12 basins, lower in 8; median difference -0.039 NSE, mean -0.118, difference of the medians -0.043 (typical seed range 0.067, Wilcoxon p = 0.519); for basins in training: no clear difference, higher with properties in 8 of 12, median difference +0.014.

2 days ahead, LSTM against the random forest, both never having seen the basin: the LSTM is higher in 2 of 12 basins with basin properties (median difference -0.040) and in 5 of 12 with weather only (-0.009).

3 days ahead, never-seen basin: median test NSE 0.092 with basin properties and 0.113 with weather only, against 0.228 when the basin was in training; 10 of 12 basins keep a positive NSE with properties, 9 of 12 with weather only, 12 of 12 for the random forest (median 0.138).

3 days ahead, loss from not having seen the basin (median over basins): +0.064 NSE with basin properties (11 of 12 basins lower, 9 by more than the typical seed range of 0.052, 10 below every single in-training seed); +0.021 with weather only (11 lower, 5 beyond the seed range); -0.009 for the random forest; largest loss 2.00 / 0.64 / 0.53.

3 days ahead, basin properties for a never-seen basin: no clear difference by the median rule - higher with properties in 4 of 12 basins, lower in 8; median difference -0.030 NSE, mean -0.097, difference of the medians -0.021 (typical seed range 0.052, Wilcoxon p = 0.470); for basins in training: no clear difference, higher with properties in 8 of 12, median difference +0.019.

3 days ahead, LSTM against the random forest, both never having seen the basin: the LSTM is higher in 3 of 12 basins with basin properties (median difference -0.043) and in 5 of 12 with weather only (-0.024).

Warnings 1 day ahead with the model's own level (pooled over 12 basins): in training 21% of onsets warned with 85% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 53% warned, 56% false); held out with properties 23% of onsets warned with 86% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 50% warned, 59% false); held out weather only 18% of onsets warned with 88% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 49% warned, 59% false); held-out forest 19% of onsets warned with 86% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 50% warned, 58% false).

Warnings 2 days ahead with the model's own level (pooled over 12 basins): in training 15% of onsets warned with 84% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 39% warned, 68% false); held out with properties 16% of onsets warned with 85% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 35% warned, 71% false); held out weather only 14% of onsets warned with 86% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 37% warned, 70% false); held-out forest 14% of onsets warned with 85% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 36% warned, 68% false).

Warnings 3 days ahead with the model's own level (pooled over 12 basins): in training 14% of onsets warned with 83% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 31% warned, 74% false); held out with properties 14% of onsets warned with 86% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 27% warned, 78% false); held out weather only 13% of onsets warned with 85% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 29% warned, 76% false); held-out forest 13% of onsets warned with 84% of those warnings false (all high-flow days: 28% warned, 75% false).

Loses most when held out - Charlie Creek, FL (Southern lowlands, 886 km2): NSE 1 day ahead -1.98 with properties, -0.68 with weather only, -0.56 for the forest, against 0.52 in training; forecast volume +185% / +109% / +102% (in training +23%); onsets warned 65% / 47% / 47% (in training 59%); properties outside the range of the other 11: aridity, geol_permeability; nearest other basin: Myakka, FL (distance 2.4); runoff ratio 0.19 (rank 12 of 12, highest first).

Loses most when held out - SF Holston, VA (Mountains, 785 km2): NSE 1 day ahead 0.35 with properties, 0.19 with weather only, 0.43 for the forest, against 0.48 in training; forecast volume +7% / +50% / +4% (in training +6%); onsets warned 34% / 22% / 24% (in training 24%); properties outside the range of the other 11: none; nearest other basin: Catawba, NC (distance 1.8); runoff ratio 0.42 (rank 4 of 12, highest first).

Loses most when held out - French Broad, NC (Mountains, 179 km2): NSE 1 day ahead 0.15 with properties, 0.32 with weather only, 0.30 for the forest, against 0.41 in training; forecast volume +41% / +6% / +7% (in training +6%); onsets warned 4% / 3% / 1% (in training 3%); properties outside the range of the other 11: p_mean, aridity; nearest other basin: South Toe, NC (distance 3.5); runoff ratio 0.57 (rank 2 of 12, highest first).

Loses most when held out - Turkey Creek, GA (Southern lowlands, 123 km2): NSE 1 day ahead 0.25 with properties, 0.44 with weather only, 0.39 for the forest, against 0.45 in training; forecast volume +2% / +26% / +40% (in training +36%); onsets warned 24% / 28% / 28% (in training 28%); properties outside the range of the other 11: none; nearest other basin: Hyco Creek, NC (distance 3.5); runoff ratio 0.24 (rank 10 of 12, highest first).

Loses most when held out - Murder Creek, GA (Northern lowlands, 491 km2): NSE 1 day ahead 0.39 with properties, 0.32 with weather only, 0.36 for the forest, against 0.54 in training; forecast volume +66% / +58% / +57% (in training +6%); onsets warned 25% / 5% / 23% (in training 23%); properties outside the range of the other 11: none; nearest other basin: Little River, NC (distance 1.1); runoff ratio 0.23 (rank 11 of 12, highest first).

Scores higher when held out - Myakka, FL: NSE 1 day ahead 0.53 with properties, 0.40 with weather only, 0.56 for the forest, against 0.25 in training (single seeds 0.14 to 0.27; forest in training 0.25). 31% of the rain reached this river in the training years and 21% in the test years (drop ranked 2 of 12, largest first). Forecast volume in the test years: +69% in training, +12% / +4% / +6% held out; in the training years: +6% in training, -25% / -32% / -29% held out. In the validation years the order is the usual one: NSE 0.57 in training, 0.42 / 0.48 / 0.48 held out. The higher score goes with a change in the river between the two periods; it is not evidence of skill for unseen rivers.

What goes with the loss (Spearman over 12 basins, 1 day ahead, with properties): distance to the nearest other basin in property space rho = +0.51 (p = 0.09); runoff ratio -0.29 (p = 0.35); basin size +0.34 (p = 0.29). Lowest held-out scores with properties: Charlie Creek, FL, French Broad, NC, Hyco Creek, NC; with weather only: Charlie Creek, FL, Hyco Creek, NC, SF Holston, VA.
notes: Protocol: for each basin, one LSTM is trained on the other 11 basins (flood.fit with ids = the 11): input scalers, flow scaler, loss weights and the early-stopping score all come from those 11 basins' training and validation years. The held-out basin's flow is never read before scoring; only its weather (and, in the first variant, its ten properties) enters the forecast.

Settings are those chosen by 04_lstm_all.py (results/lstm_all.json, key config) with the budget capped at 1000 updates and patience 4 (04: 2000 / 6). Replaying the capped stopping rule on the recorded validation curve of the in-training reference lstm_w_s0 keeps the same check (update 300), so the reference is exactly the model this budget would have produced.

7 of the 24 held-out trainings reached the limit of 1000 updates before the stopping rule was met (best_update and updates_run are in cost_per_fold); a longer budget might have changed them. The stopping point is chosen on the validation years of the 11 training basins: it measures skill in new years for basins the model knows, not skill for a new basin, so it cannot notice a model that tells its training basins apart by their properties.

That setting (hidden size, learning rate) was chosen in 04 on the validation years of all 12 basins, the held-out one included. 04 found the three candidates equal within seed noise, so this is a weak leak; a strict ungauged test would repeat the choice inside every fold.

One seed per held-out model (seed 0, as the reference lstm_w_s0). A second seed was not affordable, so every difference is set against in_training_seed_range_median: the typical spread, per basin, of the 3 seeds of the in-training model (lstm_w_s0, lstm_w_s1, lstm_w_s2). The 24 held-out models also differ in their training basins, so their own seed noise may be larger than that yardstick.

Verdict rule for the basin properties: 'help' / 'hurt' when the median over basins of (with minus without) is beyond the typical seed range, otherwise 'no clear difference'. It describes, it does not prove; nothing was chosen with it. The count of basins, the mean and the difference of the medians are given beside it because the median hides a single large failure.

in_training = lstm_w_s0 (one model for all 12 basins, past weather + basin properties). in_training_no_properties = lobo_ref_w_nostatic, one extra training of this script (all 12 basins, weather only, same seed and budget), added so that the loss of the weather-only variant is measured against a model with the same inputs. loss_* = in training minus held out (positive = worse when never seen). Measured against lstm_w_s0 instead, the median loss of the weather-only variant would be 0.060 / 0.050 / 0.034 NSE at 1 / 2 / 3 days ahead: a number that mixes 'never seen' with 'no basin properties'.

Not having seen the basin is not the only difference between a basin's two scores. In 12 of the 12 basins a smaller share of the rain reached the river in the test years than in the training years (test / training 0.66 to 0.92; key flow_per_rain), and a model trained on a river has learned the older relation: the forecast volume of lstm_w_s0 in the test years is +6% to +69% off, 1 day ahead. A held-out model never learned that relation, so where the change is large the loss measured in the test years can shrink or turn negative for a reason that has nothing to do with unseen rivers (key higher_when_held_out). flow_per_rain comes from the gauge and only describes; it is never an input.

Random forest (lobo_rf_w): one forest per held-out basin and lead on the pooled issue days of the other 11 basins; features of features.py without river flow plus the ten basin properties; fixed settings (n_estimators=100, max_samples=20000, min_samples_leaf=10, max_features=0.333, random_state=0), not tuned. The target is the flow in mm/day without per-basin weights. forest_in_training = base_rf_w of 02_baselines.py, one forest per basin fitted on that basin's own flow (leaf size tuned on validation years): a different set-up, shown for scale only.

Warnings without a gauge: a warning is given when the forecast exceeds the 95th percentile of the model's own forecasts for that basin and lead on the target days of the training years (LSTM forecasts start after the 365-day warm-up, so 19 of the 20 training years). A day counts as high flow when the observed flow exceeds the basin's observed 95th percentile of the training years (flood.thresholds) - observations are used for scoring only. Counts are pooled over the 12 basins with flood.rates. The same rule is applied to the in-training models so that the comparison is like for like.

The 'all' and 'onset' tables inside variants.<name>.test (flood.evaluate) use the observed level as the warning level - a rule an ungauged basin could not apply; they are kept for reference. Use warnings_model_level for the ungauged case.

Three of the ten basin properties (p_mean, aridity, p_seasonality) are CAMELS climate averages of 1989-2009, which overlap the validation and test years (same caveat as in lstm_all.json). No property is computed from the flow record.

worst_basins = the basins with the three largest NSE losses 1 day ahead of either LSTM variant (their union), largest loss first; lowest_held_out_nse_1_day_ahead lists the three lowest held-out scores, which also contain basins that are hard to forecast even when they are in training.

compared_with_other_11 uses the mean and spread of the other 11 basins' properties - exactly the scaling the held-out model applied. flow_record values (runoff ratio, mean flow ...) come from the gauge and are used only to describe a basin, never as an input.
All models are scored on identical days: coverage is 1.0 for every model, basin and lead in the validation and test years (asserted). The test years chose nothing.
With 12 basins (four per landscape) a median can move with a single basin; the Wilcoxon and Spearman p-values describe 12 dependent basins and are not corrected for the many comparisons.

Time under the CPU lock: 37 minutes (25 trainings 2044 s, forests 157 s), more than the 25 minutes planned. Smoke tests of other scripts do not wait for the lock, so the seconds per fold depend on what else was running and are not a clean measure of cost.

This file was written by --rescore: every score, table and note was recomputed from the saved prediction sets without training again; the per-fold training records and the timings (n_trainings, training_seconds, forest_seconds, waited_for_cpu_s, runtime_s) are those of the training run. rescore_runtime_s is the time of this pass.
